author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose missing music with working sound effects
summary: Verify the game scene and music option, cold-boot without save state, compare disc integrity and another title, and avoid global audio changes when effects already work.
heroAlt: Sakura game scene selected as a repeatable point where background music and foreground effects can be checked separately

blocks.text: Prove the game should be playing music at this point

Cold-boot the game and reach a documented scene where a track begins without loading a save state. Verify the in-game music slider, language or region settings, and that effects still play. Record the disc-image hash and inspect whether the title uses streamed audio files or disc tracks, because working sound effects only prove that the final output mixer is alive.

Do not change global latency or synchronization to recover one absent music stream. Those controls can damage every title while leaving a missing file, failed trigger, muted music bus, or stale save-state state untouched. Preserve the current memory card and use a temporary save only if reaching the test scene requires progression.
Prepare clean boot and data checks

items: Music volume and in-game audio mode recorded.
Known scene or menu with documented music available.
Memory-card save available independently from save states.
Record the game serial, image hash, music option, boot path, and exact known cue while effects and dialogue are confirmed audible.
Compare a cold boot, normal memory-card save, and suspect save state at the same trigger before inspecting streamed files or track references.

blocks.text: Separate game state, data, and output

items: 1. Confirm the title's music volume is nonzero and no jukebox option disables the track.
2. Reach the reference scene from a cold boot using a memory-card save.
3. Repeat without loading an old save state that may preserve broken game state.
4. Check whether music appears in menus, cutscenes, or another area.
5. Test a second PS2 title to confirm general streaming audio works.
6. Verify the game image against the known-good dump record.
7. Keep emulator audio synchronization unchanged while effects are already correct.
8. Document a title-specific reproduction if clean data and cold boot still fail.

blocks.text: Compare a cold boot with the suspect save state, then test another known music cue in the same game. If only the state restore is silent, recreate progress from a normal save. If every cue is missing, verify the personal dump and its track references. If one regional revision works, compare serial, patch, and data layout before blaming the audio backend.
Accept music and effects as independent checks

The expected track must start from the chosen trigger while effects and dialogue remain audible, continue through the intended transition, and return after a cold relaunch. Repeat without the diagnostic save state and verify a second game still produces music under the unchanged global audio configuration.

items: The reference scene reliably starts its expected track.
Effects remain audible and synchronized during the music test.
Cold boot and verified image produce the same healthy result.
The evidence must show whether silence follows state restoration, one cue, every music stream, a regional dump, or a patch identifier.
Cold-boot without the diagnostic state and reach two confirmed music triggers; both must start while effects remain intact under global defaults.
Music returns without save state: retire the affected state and save normally.
Only one region fails: verify that region's dump and compatibility notes.
All titles lose streaming music: capture an emulator-wide audio report.
Music exists but one channel is absent: run the stereo-channel procedure.

blocks.text: Return the title to its saved audio configuration

Discard only the temporary state or per-game audio experiment, restore the documented in-game music option, and cold-boot again. Do not overwrite the memory card or replace the entire library image until the hash and track layout have been checked. If a patch caused the fault, disable that patch and retain its identifier with the evidence.
Silence can be intentional game state

Some scenes intentionally fade, suppress, or delay music according to mission state, so an arbitrary playable area is not a valid test. Use a confirmed trigger and distinguish music data from generated effects. Compatibility notes should name the game serial, boot path, cue, dump format, and whether the failure survives a clean boot.
Review Android audio output behavior before global changes
